core: Receptor tyrosine kinase signaling to PI3K/AKT and ERK
name: Receptor tyrosine kinase PI3K/AKT and ERK signaling via IRS/SHC adaptors
rationale: All members concern tyrosine-kinase receptor phosphorylation driving PI3K/AKT and ERK outputs; the IRS, SHC and SOS adaptor events (IGF1R, ALK/LTK) distinguish it from MET/ERBB-centred and negative-feedback RAS/MAPK neighbours.

name: Sulfonation-based metabolism of steroids and xenobiotics
rationale: Members cover xenobiotic and steroid metabolism with cytosolic sulfotransferase conjugation, distinguishing it from neighbours built on CYP oxidation, acetylation and amino acid conjugation.

core: Leading-edge actin dynamics in cell motility
name: Actin filament severing, capping and crosslinking in leading-edge motility
rationale: All members regulate actin filament assembly, turnover and protrusions (ruffles, lamellipodia, pseudopodia) driving migration; the filament severing, capping, depolymerization and crosslinking members distinguish it from Arp2/3-WAVE, focal-adhesion bundle and filopodial neighbours.

qualifier: acetylation, methylation and amino acid conjugation
name: Phase II acetyl, methyl and amino acid conjugation of xenobiotics
rationale: Members are drug and aromatic-compound biotransformation steps (acetylation, methylation, glycine/glutamine conjugation, CYP2E1, paracetamol); the amino acid conjugation and acetyl/methyl transfer set it apart from drug-ADME and CYP-oxidation neighbours.

name: Type I interferon antiviral transcriptional signature
rationale: All members are interferon-alpha/antiviral gene-expression signatures (including IRF2 target networks), distinguishing them from neighbours defined by specific effectors such as ISG15 or OAS or by cytosolic DNA sensing.

name: Gluconeogenesis and glycerol, alditol and alanine metabolism
rationale: Members cover gluconeogenesis and its carbon sources (glycerol/glycerol-3-phosphate, alditols, alanine, oxaloacetate, fructose synthesis), distinguishing it from pentose-phosphate and fructose catabolism neighbours.

name: Perinatal lung maturation and epithelial cell differentiation
rationale: Members concern saccular-stage lung and perinatal events (pneumocyte, secretory and bronchial epithelial differentiation, ductus arteriosus closure), distinguishing it from surfactant-disease and branching/mesenchymal lung neighbours.

core: NK cell activation and cytotoxicity regulation
name: NK cell activation and cytotoxicity regulation via MHC class Ib
rationale: Members regulate NK and cytotoxic lymphocyte activation, degranulation and cytokine output through receptor recognition of non-lymphoid cells; MHC class Ib presentation and NK effector control distinguish it from T-cell costimulation and KIR/tolerance neighbours.

name: P4-ATPase phospholipid flipping and intermembrane PI/PC transfer
rationale: Members concern moving phospholipids across or between membranes, centred on TMEM30A-dependent aminophospholipid flippases and PI/PC transfer, distinguishing it from scramblase, glycolipid transport and ER-shaping neighbours.

core: Double-stranded RNA sensing and interferon restraint
name: Double-stranded RNA sensing by TLR3/PKR and ADAR editing
rationale: Members concern host handling of dsRNA: endosomal TLR3 pathway (and its HSE deficiencies), PKR, ADAR A-to-I editing and damping of type I IFN signaling; TLR3-HSE and ADAR editing distinguish it from broad antiviral, TLR7/8/9 and TLR3 cell-death neighbours.

name: Fibronectin-integrin matrix adhesion driving fibroblast and endothelial migration
rationale: Members cover ECM assembly (fibronectin, collagen, syndecans), integrin adhesion, focal adhesion/stress fibre formation and fibroblast/endothelial migration; the ECM matrix modules distinguish it from MET/PTK2 spreading, Rho-kinase and EMT neighbours.

name: Sperm capacitation, acrosome reaction and egg binding
rationale: All members are sperm events preparing for and achieving oocyte contact, distinguishing it from sperm motility/flagellum and maternal-to-zygotic transition neighbours.

qualifier: negative control of RIG-I and cGAS-STING
name: Interferon-beta production control with RIG-I/cGAS-STING negative regulation
rationale: Members regulate type I IFN (mainly IFN-beta) induction by nucleic-acid sensors, dominated by negative regulation of RIG-I, cGAS-STING and TREX1; this restraint distinguishes it from neighbours that activate IRF3/RIG-I/MDA5 signaling.

qualifier: organic cation and cystine, renal proximal tubule
name: Renal proximal tubule organic cation and cystine transport
rationale: Members are plasma-membrane SLC transport of organic ions, amino acids and cystine in liver/kidney epithelia; organic cation/anion, cystinuria and proximal-tubule members distinguish it from neutral amino acid and urate transport neighbours.

qualifier: capping, end protection and recombination control
name: Telomere capping, end protection and recombination control
rationale: All members concern telomere integrity; capping, protection from NHEJ and control of telomeric recombination (t-circles, D-loops) distinguish it from break-induced replication, C-strand synthesis and DNA-topology neighbours.

name: Cationic and neutral amino acid membrane transport
rationale: Members are amino acid transport events; the cationic lysine, arginine and ornithine carriers (SLC7A7, SLC25A15) distinguish it from neighbours centred on peptides, tryptophan or polyamines.

name: NGF signaling through TRKA and p75NTR
rationale: Members cover NGF processing and signaling through TRKA and p75NTR (survival, death, proteolysis), distinguishing it from BDNF/NT3 NTRK2/3 signaling and dependence-receptor death neighbours.

qualifier: oxidative lesion glycosylases and their defects
name: Oxidative DNA lesion excision by glycosylases and inherited defects
rationale: Members are glycosylase recognition and cleavage of damaged bases (OGG1, MUTYH, NTHL1, NEIL) and their defective variants, distinguishing it from alkylation reversal and long-patch gap-filling BER neighbours.

name: Dopamine receptor signaling in synaptic transmission and behavior
rationale: Members cover dopamine receptor coupling (adenylate cyclase, PLC, beta-arrestin) and dopaminergic synaptic and behavioral effects, distinguishing it from dopamine synthesis/uptake and drug-of-abuse response neighbours.

name: Centrosomal microtubule nucleation and stabilization with actin crosstalk
rationale: Members concern centrosome positioning, microtubule nucleation and stabilization plus actin-linked localization (citron kinase); these distinguish it from mitotic centrosome, centriole/cilium and spindle orientation neighbours.

name: Lung branching morphogenesis and mesenchymal proliferation
rationale: Members cover lung bud branching, lobe growth and lung mesenchyme proliferation, distinguishing it from saccular/pneumocyte, trachea/vasculature and non-lung epithelial-mesenchymal neighbours.

qualifier: routed to lysosomal degradation over recycling
name: Receptor internalization and lysosomal degradation over recycling
rationale: Members promote receptor endocytosis (including GPCRs, clathrin cargo recognition) and lysosomal catabolism while inhibiting recycling, distinguishing it from recycling/surface-retention, caveolar and LDLR-specific neighbours.

name: Vitamin K-dependent gamma-carboxylation and vitamin C metabolism
rationale: Members concern vitamin K metabolism and gamma-carboxylation of protein precursors plus ascorbate metabolism and response, distinguishing it from vitamin E/ubiquinone, vitamin D and retinoid neighbours.

name: Sphingolipid metabolism and ER contact-site lipid transfer
rationale: Members cover sphingolipid/ceramide synthesis, catabolism and homeostasis plus non-vesicular lipid transfer and ER-plasma membrane tethering, distinguishing it from glycerophospholipid, lysosomal glycosphingolipid and Golgi vesicle traffic neighbours.

core: Aromatic amino acid and histidine catabolism
name: Phenylalanine, tyrosine and histidine catabolism with BH4 synthesis
rationale: Members are phenylalanine/tyrosine and histidine degradation (including phenylketonuria and formate) with BH4 cofactor synthesis, distinguishing it from generic amino acid and proline/threonine/glycine catabolism neighbours.
